about: One human player plays single points against one AI opponent. The player stands stationary at the center baseline swinging a physical M5 IMU racket controller while a webcam tracks their stroke side (forehand/backhand) and swing path. Because player court movement is fixed, focus habit reads and counter-strategies on the player shot_type (topspin, slice, dropshot), side (forehand, backhand), swing_start tells (early_guess, backswing, initial_speed), and shot placement (lands): low slice to backhand disrupts heavy topspin habits, short dropshots/slices disrupt pure topspin grinders, and moving in (middle_short / anticipate move_in) with flat drives punishes dropshot habits. Serves are topspin, flat, or slice. Message timestamps t measure active play time in seconds.
goal: Start beatable. Work out what this player relies on to win points and take it away, one habit at a time, until the player wins about half the points. Win by choosing better shots, never by hitting harder or faster.

opponent.about: The AI tennis player on the far side of the net.

shot_type.when: Each time the opponent hits the ball.

options.topspin: Heavy arcing topspin with high bounce and strong margin.
options.flat: Fast, low, penetrating drive that rushes the player timing.
options.slice: Low-skidding backspin ball that stays low and forces upward lift.
options.dropshot: Soft, short ball landing just over the net that punishes deep positioning.
options.lob: High deep arc over the player head that resets the rally or punishes forward reach.

aim.when: Each time the opponent hits the ball.

options.left_deep: Deep to the left side of the player half (right-hander backhand side).
options.middle_deep: Deep down the middle of the player baseline.
options.right_deep: Deep to the right side of the player half (right-hander forehand side).
options.left_short: Short angle to the left side near the service line.
options.right_short: Short angle to the right side near the service line.

position.when: Right after the opponent hits the ball.

options.middle_deep: Recover to the middle of the far baseline.
options.left_deep: Shade left on the far baseline to cover shots to screen-left.
options.right_deep: Shade right on the far baseline to cover shots to screen-right.
options.middle_short: Step forward toward the net to take the next ball early.

anticipate.when: The moment the player starts a swing (~100-160ms before ball contact).

options.stay: Hold current position until the ball is hit.
options.move_in: Start moving forward toward the net to cover a short ball.
options.move_back: Start moving deeper behind the baseline.

swing_start.about: The player started a swing (~85-160ms before ball contact). High reliability on side and arm_zone (~92%); medium-high on backswing, initial_speed, and early_guess (~75-80% match with final shot — compare with shot to spot disguised tells).

confidence.about: Reliable. Classifier confidence in early_guess before contact.

backswing.about: Reliable. Pre-swing windup/takeback size (0 = compact/no windup, 1 = big windup).

initial_speed.about: Reliable. Swing onset speed in first 25ms (separates gentle dropshot taps from hard drives).

anticipate.about: The opponent reacted to swing_start before ball contact.

shot.about: Either side hit the ball (emitted once per shot at racket-ball contact with solved landing zone and result). High-reliability labels: side, arm_zone, shot_type, timing, from, lands, result. For shot direction, use lands rather than angle.

power.about: High reliability. Normalized swing effort from M5 peak dynamic accel + gyro (0 = soft touch, 1 = max rip).

rotation.about: Medium-high reliability (slightly noisy near 0). Spin from webcam vertical path + racket face; below -0.25 is slice, above +0.2 is topspin.

angle.about: Noisy (gyro yaw can drift if feet shift mid-point) — weight lightly; use lands zone for shot direction.

confidence.about: High reliability. Classifier + pose confidence in the shot_type and side labels.

quality.about: High reliability. Contact quality from lateral/depth reach and ball height (low when stretched or jammed, high when comfortable).

missed_swing.about: High reliability. The player physically swung the racket during a rally and missed the ball (strong signal of being fooled by a dropshot or stretched out of reach).

power.about: High reliability. Effort of the missed swing.

swing_backswing.about: Reliable. How big the player backswing was on the latest swing_start (passed to anticipate and to the opponent return picks on that shot).

swing_initial_speed.about: Reliable. How fast the player swing started in the first 25ms on the latest swing_start (passed to anticipate and to the opponent return picks on that shot).

views.court: Broadcast view of both halves of the tennis court showing player, AI opponent, and ball positions (3D stadium court, or 2D tactical court fallback).
views.player_cam: Unmirrored webcam on the player showing upper body and racket arm.

opponent_speed.about: Fairness dial controlling how quickly the AI opponent split-steps, sprints across the court, and sets its feet before hitting (0.65 = sluggish/error-prone under pace, 0.85 = balanced default, 1.25 = fast/rock-solid wall; never changes ball speed).

forehand_lover.about: Hits about 70% forehands, mostly cross-court. Weak on deep balls to the backhand.

baseline_grinder.about: Stays deep behind the baseline and hits heavy topspin. Struggles with short dropshots.

even.about: Balanced player with no strong habit. Spreads shots evenly.
